paper_summary: Japanese-language 1991 study (Journal of Japan Institute of Light Metals 41(1) 44-48) of SBAC, a metal matrix syntactic foam made by pressure-infiltrating molten Al-12%Si casting alloy (AC3A, melted at 973 K) into packed beds of shirasu (volcanic glass) balloons, using two balloon series (A and B) of differing specific gravity in five sieve fractions from 105 to 590 um. SBAC fails in a brittle manner, the crack running through the equatorial planes of the balloons and the most constricted matrix sections; the effective area fractions there are AM = 0.363 - 0.282*VSB and ASG = (1.28 + 0.556*VSB)*h/R, and because the shirasu glass shell (E about 70 GPa) and the Al alloy (E about 72 GPa) have nearly equal Young's moduli, tensile strength is proportional to AM + ASG. Extrapolating to AM + ASG = 1 gives 123 MPa (A-type) and 140 MPa (B-type); the difference is attributed to the lower sphericity of A-type balloons raising the stress concentration factor (alpha about 2.6 vs 2.3), which implies a shirasu glass strength of about 320 MPa versus 196 MPa for the matrix alloy.

processing.matrix_name: Al-12%Si casting aluminium alloy (JIS AC3A), density 2.66 g/cm3, tensile strength 196 MPa
processing.particle_grade: Shirasu balloon (volcanic glass microballoon) from Furue, Kagoshima; type A (one of two series differing in specific gravity, made by varying foaming temperature and time), sieve fraction 105～149 um

structure.microstructure_notes: SB packed bed pressure-infiltrated with the melt; macroscopically homogeneous SBAC with almost no misrun or shrinkage cavity. Fracture is brittle and runs through the equatorial planes of the balloons and the most constricted matrix sections between contacting balloons. Some balloon walls are broken during casting and the melt penetrates inside them (breakage fraction FSB), and the point-count method double-counts those regions so that VSB + VM exceeds 1. Densities calculated by the rule of mixtures are systematically higher than the measured SBAC densities because the air-comparison specific gravity of SB overestimates its true specific gravity. FSB for this composition is stated only as being 10% or below; the value is in Table 1, which is not present in the extracted text.

test.specimen_notes: Instron-type universal testing machine, crosshead speed 8.3 um/s, 10 specimens per condition; flat tensile coupon machined from the plate cut parallel to the casting base (Fig. 1(b),(c)), taken from within 20 mm of the base where the density was uniform. Test temperature is not stated in the paper.

evidence.quote: SBは鹿児島県古江産のシラスで発泡温度と時間を調整し, 比重が異なる2系統のものを粒径が105～149, 149～210, 210～297, 297～420, 420～590μmの5段階にふるい分けて用いた。
一方, 基地金属にはAl-12%Si系鋳造用アルミニウム合金 (AC3A) を用いた。
この金型を所定温度に予熱した後, 973Kで溶解した320gのAl-12%Si合金 (AC3A) 溶湯を注湯する。そして, この溶湯(G)を黒鉛パンチ(H)を介してプレス(I)にて加圧しSB充填層内に圧入後冷却すればSBACができ上がる。
引張試験片は Fig. 1(b)の板材から(c)に示す形状と寸法に加工した。引張試験はインストロン型万能試験機を用い, クロスヘッド速度8.3μm/sで行った。試験本数は10本である。
Table 1にSBACの比重ρSBAC, SBの体積分率VSBと基地金属の体積分率VMおよびSBの破壊率FSBを示す。 … Table 1にSBACの引張強さσSBACを示す。
evidence.location: Sec. 3.1 / 3.2 - the per-sample values (rho_SBAC, VSB, VM, FSB, sphericity, sigma_SBAC) are in Table 1, whose contents are missing from the extracted text

structure.microstructure_notes: SB packed bed pressure-infiltrated with the melt; macroscopically homogeneous SBAC with almost no misrun or shrinkage cavity. Fracture is brittle and runs through the equatorial planes of the balloons and the most constricted matrix sections between contacting balloons. Some balloon walls are broken during casting and the melt penetrates inside them (breakage fraction FSB), and the point-count method double-counts those regions so that VSB + VM exceeds 1. Densities calculated by the rule of mixtures are systematically higher than the measured SBAC densities because the air-comparison specific gravity of SB overestimates its true specific gravity. FSB for this composition is stated only as being 10% or below; the value is in Table 1, which is not present in the extracted text.

extraction_notes: IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this is a genuine hollow-glass-microballoon / aluminium syntactic foam paper, but the OCR'd text contains only the CAPTION of Table 1 ('Specific characteristics of SB and SBAC'), not its contents. Table 1 holds every per-sample number - SB air-comparison specific gravity rho_SB, SEM-measured wall thickness hS, SBAC specific gravity rho_SBAC, SB and matrix volume fractions VSB and VM, breakage fraction FSB, sphericity, and the measured tensile strengths sigma_SBAC - and Figs. 3 and 5 hold the load-displacement and strength-vs-area-fraction data. None of those could be read, so the ten fabricated compositions (2 balloon series x 5 sieve fractions) carry null properties, null volume fraction and null density. Nothing was estimated off the plots. Two extra records are marked data_origin='model': the Fig. 5 extrapolations of tensile strength to AM + ASG = 1 (123 MPa for A-type, 140 MPa for B-type). These are analytical extrapolations, not measured compositions, which is stated in their sample_label; alpha = 2.6 (A) and 2.3 (B) and sigma_SG about 320 MPa are the associated derived values. particle_breakage_fraction is filled only for A 420-590 um SBAC (FSB = 11.3%, the one value stated in running text); all other compositions are described only as '10% or below'. particle_mean_diameter_um is left null because the paper gives sieve ranges (105-149, 149-210, 210-297, 297-420, 420-590 um) and uses a mean radius R taken from Table 1, which is unavailable; the ranges are recorded in particle_grade. cure_or_process_temperature_c = 700 C is the stated melt temperature (973 K); the die preheat was 623-673 K (350-400 C), the melt injection speed 1.0-2.2 cm/s and the maximum hydrostatic pressure 1.4-5.1 MPa (ranges, so not entered as single values). Test temperature is not stated anywhere, so temperature_c is null rather than assumed to be 25 C, and no gauge length is given for the 8.3 um/s crosshead speed so strain_rate_per_s is null. The unreinforced Al-12%Si matrix tensile strength (196 MPa) and the shirasu glass shell strength (about 320 MPa, back-calculated) are constituent properties, not syntactic-foam records, so they appear in matrix_name / notes rather than as records. Note on typing: shirasu balloons are hollow volcanic aluminosilicate glass and this paper explicitly calls them hollow glass microspheres ('volcano glass micro-balloons'), so particle_type = glass_microballoon here.
